text:
julia.sre: heads-up: apiserver 5xx spike in eu-west1 ~08:22 UTC. etcd leader CPU ~95% and raft heartbeats delayed. started when provisioner ramped a large GPU attach batch. anyone tracking?

mike: on it, pulling apiserver + etcd logs. any idea which customers affected?

sam.provisioner: we started a reserved-capacity attach batch at 08:20 to satisfy queued allocs. attach rate peaked ~120/s for ~30s. seeing conntrack DROPPED counters on nat-gw. suspect SNAT exhaustion.

deploy-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0113 apiserver-degraded-eu-west1 (priority P2)

anya-ml: if we can throttle the attach rate short-term can we route traffic to cached/quantized model variants to reduce apiserver QPS? low-friction mitigation.

carl: running some quick checks:
```
kubectl -n kube-system logs etcd-eu-west1 -c etcd | grep -i raft | tail -n 30
kubectl get nodes -o wide && kubectl get endpoints kube-apiserver -o wide
```
short log snippet:
```
W0312 08:22:31.123 apiserver request.go:123] 500 GET /api/v1/namespaces/...: read tcp 10.0.0.1:443->10.1.2.3:56231: i/o timeout
etcdserver: leader CPU 94% raft tick delayed
```

julia.sre: sam, can you pause or throttle the attach jobs? maybe set provisioner.maxBurst to 10/s and gate the rest.

sam.provisioner: pausing the current batch now. reducing burst to 8/s and applying a temporary rate-limit patch (rolling). will update in ~2m.

mike: confirmed conntrack table on nat-gw-02 at 65535/65535. ephemeral port exhaustion. we can increase conntrack size or expand ephemeral port range but that's an infra change and slower.

anya-ml: :thumbsup: routing non-critical inference traffic to model-light for 15m to trim QPS by ~30%. will monitor.

julia.sre: noted. cost caveat: adding more NAT gateways or dedicated NAT capacity per region will add ~ $800/mo per gateway — will need finance sign-off for permanent capacity.

sam.provisioner: attach batch paused; observing apiserver error-rate decline. spike window ~3m. rolling back aggressive autoscale rule that allowed big bursts.

carl: apiserver 5xxs back to baseline. etcd leader CPU down to ~40%. logs look normal. immediate action items for postmortem:
- enforce attach rate limits in provisioner with hard caps
- add conntrack saturation alert to SRE runbook + dashboards
- consider dedicated NAT capacity for gpu-onboard flows in high-attach regions
- evaluate cost vs reliability (reserve NAT vs throttle behavior)

julia.sre: adding to postmortem doc and scheduling a follow-up with infra/cost/product tomorrow 10:00 UTC. thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:

mike: will keep monitor up and close incident after 30m stable.
